newsitem.title: CANADA: Atlantic film to open Toronto film festival series.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic film to open Toronto film festival series.

text.p: The Toronto International Film Festival said on Tuesday the world premiere of the Atlantic Canadian film "The Hanging Garden" will open Perspective Canada, the festival series dedicated to Canadian film.

The decision marks the first time a movie from Atlantic Canada has opened the series. This year Perspective Canada will include 20 feature films, including a gala presentation of Atom Egoyan's "The Sweet Hereafter", which won the runner-up Grand Jury Prize at Cannes.
"The Hanging Garden" is the story of a young gay man who returns to his rural Nova Scotia home after a bitter absence of 10 years. The movie is the feature debut of director Thom Fitzgerald.

"We are first of all very surprised but we're extremely honored. We can't be more thrilled," the film's producer, Louise Garfield, told Reuters. "It represents some of the great activity that's going on in Atlantic Canada. It's like a wave."

Other features include "Drive, She Said" by "Double Happiness" director Mina Shum, "The Planet of Junior Brown", directed by Clement Virgo, and "Uncut" by John Greyson, whose film "Lilies" last year beat out "Crash" to win the Canada's top award for film.

The Perspective Canada series, which in the past has included such provocative fare as the necrophiliac love story "Kissed", will also include the world premiere of "A Sexual Woman Is..", a feature-length documentary about what turns women on.
Thirty-one short films on topics ranging from a profile of an Iroquois photographer to a fictional account of the 1919 Winnipeg general strike will also be included in the series.
"It sounds good. It sounds like a lot of first films," said director Virgo, whose has brought two other films including his feature "Rude" to previous festivals.
Organizers of the series also announced a new award for the best Canadian first feature film. The award, worth C$15,000 ($10,800), is sponsored by CHUM Ltd's Citytv.
